## codegraph
# Codegraph — code intelligence over an indexed knowledge graph

Codegraph is a SQLite knowledge graph of every symbol, edge, and file in
the workspace — pre-computed structure you would otherwise re-derive by
reading files (cached intelligence: thousands of parse/trace decisions you
don't pay to re-reason each run). Reads are sub-millisecond; the index lags
writes by ~1s through the file watcher. Reach for it BEFORE *and* while
writing or editing code — not just for questions: one call returns the
verbatim source PLUS who calls it and what it affects, so you edit with the
blast radius in view. More accurate context, in far fewer tokens and
round-trips than reading files yourself.

## One tool: codegraph_explore — use it instead of reading files

There is a single tool, `codegraph_explore`, and it is Read-equivalent. It
takes either a natural-language question or a bag of symbol/file names and
returns the **verbatim, line-numbered source** of the relevant symbols
grouped by file — the same `<n>\t<line>` shape `Read` gives you, safe to
`Edit` from — PLUS the call path among them (including dynamic-dispatch hops
like callbacks, React re-render, and JSX children that grep can't follow) and
a blast-radius summary of what depends on them.

Whether you're answering "how does X work" or implementing a change (fixing a
bug, adding a feature), call `codegraph_explore` before you Read. ONE call
usually answers the whole question. Codegraph IS the pre-built search index —
so running your own grep + read loop, or delegating the lookup to a separate
file-reading sub-task/agent, repeats work codegraph already did and costs more
for the same answer. A direct codegraph answer is typically one to a few
calls; a grep/read exploration is dozens.

## How to query

- **Almost any question — "how does X work", architecture, a bug, "what/where is X", or surveying an area** → `codegraph_explore` with a natural-language question or the relevant names. ONE capped call returns the verbatim source grouped by file; most often the ONLY call y… [truncated]

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. 30			config.ClientSecret:            "clientSecret",

43	}

45	// ExchangeToken returns the exchanged OAuth2 token using the given authorization code.
46	// If codeVerifier is provided, it will be used for PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) validation.
47	func (p *IdentityProvider) ExchangeToken(ctx context.Context, redirectURL, code, codeVerifier string) (string, error) {
48		conf := &oauth2.Config{
49			ClientID:     p.config.ClientId,
50			ClientSecret: p.config.ClientSecret,
51			RedirectURL:  redirectURL,
52			Scopes:       p.config.Scopes,
53			Endpoint: oauth2.Endpoint{
54				AuthURL:   p.config.AuthUrl,
55				TokenURL:  p.config.TokenUrl,
56				AuthStyle: oauth2.AuthStyleAutoDetect,
57			},
58		}
59	
60		// Prepare token exchange options
61		opts := []oauth2.AuthCodeOption{}
62	
63		// Add PKCE code_verifier if provided
64		if codeVerifier != "" {
65			opts = append(opts, oauth2.SetAuthURLParam("code_verifier", codeVerifier))
66		}
67	
68		token, err := conf.Exchange(ctx, code, opts...)
69		if err != nil {
70			return "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to exchange access token")
71		}
72	
73		// Use the standard AccessToken field instead of Extra()
74		// This is more reliable across different OAuth providers
75		if token.AccessToken == "" {
76			return "", errors.New("missing access token from authorization response")
77		}
78	
79		return token.AccessToken, nil
80	}

82	// UserInfo returns the parsed user information using the given OAuth2 token.
83	func (p *IdentityProvider) UserInfo(ctx context.Context, token string) (*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo, error) {
84		client := &http.Client{Timeout: userInfoRequestTimeout}
85		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, p.config.UserInfoUrl, nil)
86		if err != nil {
87			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create http request")
88		}
89		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
90		req.Header.Set("Authorization", fmt.Sprintf("Bearer %s", token))
91		resp, err := client.Do(req)
92		if err != nil {
93			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get user information")
94		}
95		defer resp.Body.Close()
96	
97		if resp.StatusCode < http.StatusOK || resp.StatusCode >= http.StatusMultipleChoices {
98			body, readErr := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 4096))
99			if readErr != nil {
100				return nil, errors.Wrap(readErr, "failed to read error response body")
101			}
102			return nil, errors.Errorf("userinfo request failed with status %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, string(body))
103		}
104	
105		body, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
106		if err != nil {
107			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read response body")
108		}
109	
110		var claims map[string]any
111		if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &claims); err != nil {
112			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to unmarshal response body")
113		}
114		userInfo := &idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo{}
115		if v, ok := claims[p.config.FieldMapping.Identifier].(string); ok {
116			userInfo.Identifier = v
117		}
118		if userInfo.Identifier == "" {
119			return nil, errors.Errorf("the field %q is not found in claims or has empty value", p.config.FieldMapping.Identifier)
120		}
121	
122		// Best effort to map optional fields
123		if p.config.FieldMapping.DisplayName != "" {
124			if v, ok := claims[p.config.FieldMapping.DisplayName].(string); ok {
125				userInfo.DisplayName = v
126			}
127		}
128		if userInfo.DisplayName == "" {
129			userInfo.DisplayName = userInfo.Identifier
130		}
131		if p.config.FieldMapping.Email != "" {
132			if v, ok := claims[p.config.FieldMapping.Email].(string); ok {
133				userInfo.Email = v
134			}
135		}
136		if p.config.FieldMapping.AvatarUrl != "" {

content.text:
h03.
`internal/idp`; `internal/idp/oauth2`

**Abstraction — `internal/idp`** (`internal/idp/idp.go`): a single-file package defining the provider-agnostic contract, the `IdentityProviderUserInfo` struct (`Identifier`, `DisplayName`, `Email`, `AvatarURL`) that every provider normalizes remote user data into. Note it is a shared data type, not a Go interface — there is no `IdentityProvider` interface, so dispatch is done by an explicit type switch rather than polymorphism.

**Implementation — `internal/idp/oauth2`** (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`): the only concrete protocol that ships. Its header comment reads "Package oauth2 implements the OAuth2 identity provider integration." It wraps `golang.org/x/oauth2`, holds a `*storepb.OAuth2Config`, and exposes `NewIdentityProvider`, `ExchangeToken` (with PKCE `code_verifier` support), and `UserInfo`, which maps the userinfo endpoint's JSON onto `idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo` via the configured `FieldMapping`.

Supporting evidence that OAuth2 is the sole implementation:
- `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:119-121` — the only consumer, gated on `if identityProvider.Type == storepb.IdentityProvider_OAUTH2`. There is no other branch, so a provider of any other type would fall through with a nil `userInfo`.
- `proto/store/idp.proto` — the `IdentityProvider.Type` enum has only `TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` and `OAUTH2`, and `IdentityProviderConfig`'s oneof has just `oauth2_config`. No SAML or dedicated OIDC type exists (OIDC providers are configured as generic OAuth2 endpoints).
